I am a woman of 48 years, and I never went to school. I farm this maize plot like my mother taught me. I have cattle at home, so I carry their manure to the field before the rains come — that is what keeps my soil strong. For fertilizer from the shop, I try to get one bag of DAP from the cooperative when they bring it, because my neighbors who use it get more maize, but urea is expensive and sometimes the bag comes too late, so I use only a little. I keep seed from last year's harvest like always — the shop seed costs too much and I do not trust it when the rain is poor. My sons and I do the weeding ourselves; only at planting and harvest do I call two or three people from the village to help for a few days.
